title: Items inside a menu that has `withSearchBox` become first in the list after refinement
body:
**Bug: What is the current behavior?**
1. Go to react-instantsearch [storybook](https://community.algolia.com/react-instantsearch/storybook/?selectedKind=Menu&selectedStory=with%20search%20inside%20items&full=0&down=1&left=1&panelRight=1&downPanel=storybooks%2Fstorybook-addon-knobs)
2. Notice `Textiles & Rugs` is second in the list of items
3. Click `Textiles & Rugs`
4. Notice `Textiles & Rugs` order is changed and now appears first in the list. 

**Bug: What is the expected behavior?**
I'd expect the item order to be retained after refinement. At least thats whats happens with menu's that don't have `withSearchBox`.

--
Thank you for this excellent package.

comments.body:
Hi @lkbr, thanks for sharing your feedback. 

If I recall correctly we are putting the selected values at the top even for the Menu to make sure they're going to appear. 

Let's say the user find a category that has a count under all those already displayed, the selected category will not appear if the sort is only on count:desc because the limit will be applied. 

What would be the behaviour you would have expect on that case? Having an extra category displayed?

> Let's say the user find a category that has a count under all those already displayed, the selected category will not appear if the sort is only on count:desc because the limit will be applied.

Good point. I did not consider that case.

> What would be the behaviour you would have expect on that case? Having an extra category displayed?

I think you've handled it well considering your point above. But perhaps a selected item should only bubble to the top if it was not initially visible?

Lets say on load the visible category list is A, B, C and X, Y, Z are hidden.

The current behaviour completely makes sense if a user searches for Z and selects Z. 

However, its *mildly* disorientating for a user who has not *yet* searched inside a category who selects C and has the C and A swap positions on selection. 

Its a very minor issue but the difference in ordering is slightly noticeable when you have two menus (one with internal search and one without) on one page.

That might introduce complexities that are not worth it though, so happy to close this if it doesn't make sense to you.

It'll probably complexify things for sure, but i'll keep this open for now. I believe it deserves some thought until we came up with a good solution or we decide to close this :)

By curiosity, is your website showcasing the two menu accessible? I'd love to see the UI in action.

Sounds good. 

It's not yet live but I'll try to remember to post it back here when it is!

I've really enjoyed working with your Connectors api. Thank you.

The behavior is inconsistent with other flavors (no other flavor has a searchable `<Menu>` but it's the same with `<RefinementList>`). Keeping the order when the menu is searchable is not perfect but that's what we defaulted to. We might at least want to be consistent.
